method: npx lighthouse (v13.4.0), headless Chrome, --only-categories=performance, against live production, no throttling override (Lighthouse default simulated throttling).
verdict: FAIL against the internal budget documented in AIWMC_QUANTIS_PRODUCTION_STABILIZATION_MASTER_PLAN.md section 20.3 (LCP <= 2.5s target)

root_cause_analysis.finding: TTFB is fast (50-200ms) on every route -- the server/CDN is not the bottleneck. LCP is delayed 6+ seconds by main-thread JS execution before the page can paint, not by network or server latency.
root_cause_analysis.evidence: Lighthouse bootup-time audit on '/': ui-vendor-BuUXtMtA.js alone consumes 4494ms total main-thread time (2339ms pure scripting); index-fqbGfqma.js consumes 1846ms. Combined script evaluation across all main-thread work: 2924ms.
root_cause_analysis.consistent_with: Vite's own build-time warning (observed during 'bun run build' earlier this session): 'Some chunks are larger than 500 kB after minification... Consider dynamic import() / manualChunks' -- flagged for ui-vendor (262.60 kB min), DocumentEditor (638.13 kB), index (901.84 kB), and pdf (1,470.08 kB) chunks. This performance audit is the first time that build-time warning has been connected to a measured live-production symptom.
root_cause_analysis.cls_note: CLS is 0 across all three routes -- no layout-shift problem. This is specifically a JS-bootup/hydration blocking issue, not a rendering-stability issue.

not_yet_done: No code changes made this pass. Fixing this requires a code-splitting/manualChunks strategy (vite.config.ts) plus dynamic import() conversions for heavy, non-critical-path modules (DocumentEditor, pdf export). That is a build-configuration change with real regression risk (chunk-loading order, lazy-load fallbacks) and belongs in its own scoped slice with its own build+test+live-verify cycle, not bundled into a measurement pass.
